title: Restricted opposite-unipotent freeness of the Steinberg Weyl module
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and such that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that iterated commutator subgroup schemes become trivial, and finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with unipotent radical $U$, projection $\pi_T:B\to T$, character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, and coroot pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. A split torus is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; Borel means maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup, and the unipotent radical is the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Put $Q=S/B$ and $N=|\Phi^+|$. For $\mu\in X$ let $M_\mu=\mathcal L_{-\mu\circ\pi_T}$ be the homogeneous invertible sheaf for the action $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\mu(\pi_T(b))z)$ [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections]. Let $w_0$ be the longest Weyl element [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit]. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$ [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules], $\eta=(p-1)\rho$, and $V=\Gamma(Q,M_\eta)$ with left translation. Let $D=V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_F(V,F)$ with contragredient action $(g\ell)(v)=\ell(g^{-1}v)$. Let $U^-$ be the unipotent radical of the opposite Borel containing $T$ (its roots are $-\Phi^+$); for a representative $n_0$ of $w_0$, it is $n_0Un_0^{-1}$. Define $u(\operatorname{Lie}(U^-))$ as the quotient of its tensor algebra by $xy-yx-[x,y]$ and $x^p-x^{[p]}$, where the restricted operation is the $p$th iterate of invariant derivations. There exists a nonzero vector $d_+\in D$ fixed by $U$, with $T$ acting by $\eta$, for which
$$u(\operatorname{Lie}(U^-))\longrightarrow D,\qquad a\longmapsto a d_+$$
is an isomorphism of left $u(\operatorname{Lie}(U^-))$-modules. Here the algebra acts by the differentiated rational action. This includes the trivial group. No isomorphism between a Frobenius pushforward and a trivial bundle is asserted.

source.place: Theorem 2.6(i), printed pp.156--157: the Weyl module A((p-1)rho) is free of rank one over u(u^-), generated by its highest-weight vector. The proof there uses the lowest PBW weight and the Frobenius-algebra pairing, before Kempf vanishing and the Weyl character formula. WANTED: not stored in literature/. Read online at https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf; all-characteristic semisimple version includes products of simple factors.

proof.text: The rho identities give $\langle\eta,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=p-1$ and $-w_0\eta=\eta$. Apply [lem-sfb-induced-dual-lowest-distribution-generator] at $\eta$: its section module is exactly $V$, so $D=H w$ for a nonzero vector $w$ of weight $-\eta$, where $H=\operatorname{Dist}(U)$, and $D_i^{(b)}w=0$ for $b\geq p$. The same statement supplies finite dimensionality and the precise contragredient action.

source.place: Lemma 2.3, printed p.155; rho convention before Theorem 2.6, p.156

proof.text: Let $A_+=u(\operatorname{Lie}(U))$. Its differentiated action on $D$ exists by [lem-sfb-unipotent-restricted-enveloping-augmentation]. Its image is exactly the Lie-generated algebra in [lem-sfb-borel-simple-root-distribution-calculus]. Put $E=A_+w$. For an element $a$ of this image, the latter node gives $D_i^{(n)}aw=\sum_{r+b=n}C_{i,r}(a)D_i^{(b)}w$. Terms with $b\geq p$ vanish; for $b<p$, $D_i^{(b)}=e_i^b/b!$ and $C_{i,r}(a)$ is still in the image. Thus $E$ is stable under every $D_i^{(n)}$, hence under their algebra $H$. Since $D=Hw$, we obtain $D=A_+w$. No identification of $A_+$ with the distribution subalgebra is required.

source.place: Lemma 2.3 proof, printed p.155, expanding the divided-power stability calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-restricted-pbw-top-pairing] to $B$. The spanning vectors $e_1^{a_1}\cdots e_N^{a_N}w$ have weights $-\eta+\sum a_i\alpha_i$ (here the $\alpha_i$ enumerate all positive roots). In particular no weight is below $-\eta$. Put $d_+=n_0w\ne0$. Since $w_0\eta=-\eta$, its weight is $\eta$. Differentiating conjugation by $n_0$ sends $\operatorname{Lie}(U)$, its brackets and its restricted operation to those of $U^-$; hence it gives an algebra isomorphism $A_+\to A_-=u(\operatorname{Lie}(U^-))$ and $n_0(aw)=\operatorname{Ad}(n_0)(a)d_+$. Thus $D=A_-d_+$, and all weights of $D$ are $\eta-\sum a_i\alpha_i$ with $0\leq a_i<p$.

source.place: Theorem 1.2, p.149; Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 2.6 proof, pp.155--157; conjugation written out

proof.text: The vector $d_+$ is fixed by the group $U$, not merely its Lie algebra. For a positive root $\alpha$ expand the rational action as $x_\alpha(t)d_+=\sum_{n\geq0}t^nv_n$. The conjugation identity in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] says that $v_n$ has weight $\eta+n\alpha$. For $n>0$ this is excluded by the weight bound in step 3, because positive roots have nonnegative simple-root coordinates and are nonzero; hence $v_n=0$. The constant coefficient is $d_+$. The root product isomorphism [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] therefore gives fixation by every element of $U$ after every scalar extension. Weight comparisons here are comparisons of torus characters, not their differentials: distinct Laurent monomials in $F[T]$ are linearly independent.

source.place: Theorem 2.6 highest-vector convention, pp.156--157; root-group argument supplied explicitly from the cited root coordinates

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-restricted-pbw-top-pairing] to the opposite Borel. Its top monomial $z$ has weight $-(p-1)\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha=-2\eta$, and this weight space is $Fz$. The surjection $\phi:A_-\to D$, $a\mapsto ad_+$, shifts weights by $\eta$. The nonzero vector $w$ has weight $-\eta$, so the $-2\eta$ part of any preimage of $w$ maps to $w$. Consequently $zd_+\ne0$. Weight components may be selected since the PBW basis consists of weight vectors and distinct Laurent characters are independent.

source.place: Theorem 2.6 proof, printed pp.156--157, lowest-weight calculation

proof.text: Let $I=\ker\phi$. It is a left ideal, stable under $T$ because $d_+$ is a weight vector. If $0\ne y\in I$, the pairing in [lem-sfb-restricted-pbw-top-pairing] gives $b\in A_-$ with $L(by)\ne0$. Since $by\in I$, its $-2\eta$ weight component $L(by)z$ is in $I$. To justify selecting that component even in characteristic $p$, expand the coaction in the Laurent monomial basis of $F[T]$: stability of $I$ puts every coefficient in $I$. Thus $z\in I$, contradicting step 5. Therefore $\phi$ is injective as well as surjective. Associativity gives $\phi(ba)=b\phi(a)$, so it is the required left-module isomorphism. If $S=1$, the same calculation has $A_-=F$, $z=1$ and $D=Fw$; no nonempty root set was used.

source.place: Corollary 1.3, p.149, and Theorem 2.6 proof, pp.156--157, annihilator argument

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-5527abd2e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node lem-sfb-restricted-pbw-top-pairing and all 8 cited statements in full. Mathieu (WANTED, not stored locally) was not fetched, so I checked each step myself against the cited statements. Step 1: the rho-orbit node gives <eta,alpha_i^vee>=p-1 and -w0 eta=eta, so the dual-lowest-generator node at eta gives D=Hw with D_i^(n)w=0 for n>=p. Step 2: the divided-power commutation formula, with C_{i,r}(a) in A and D_i^(b)=e_i^b/b! for b<p, makes Aw stable under H, so D=A_+w. Step 3: PBW weights plus n0-conjugation give D=A_-d_+ with weights eta-sum a_i beta_i. Step 4: the conjugation identity puts v_n in weight eta+n alpha, which no weight of D has, because positive roots have nonnegative simple-root coefficients. The root-product scheme isomorphism then gives U-fixation over every R. Step 5: the top weight of A_- is -2eta with weight space Fz, so zd_+ is nonzero. Step 6: the T-stable left-ideal kernel, the top pairing and weight-component extraction force z into the kernel if it is nonzero, contradicting step 5. All of this is correct, and steps 2-6 really are elementary. The new node is true: restricted PBW, monomial weights, unique top weight, and nondegeneracy via gr = S(u)/(x^p) with the leading-term argument. I tested it on N=0, SL2, p=2 and products. It does not restate the item, and an rg -L DAG search finds no duplicate. No cycle and no SGA citation. Batch-5: the four listed citations reach only the generic Mathlib-type nodes lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change and lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection, which are outside the trace formula and Poincare duality and their proofs, so I accept them. No fixes and no tool_uses. Advisory: store the Mathieu PDF.
